topic: Five Guys on National Cheeseburger Day
caption: "five guys" — 100,000+ searches this week. Swipe for 10 things most people don't know about the burger chain that never discounts, except today.
Why: September 18 is National Cheeseburger Day, and Five Guys is running a rare buy-one-get-one-free burger deal, September 16 to 18, online only, code BOGOBURGER.

What most people don't know: in 1986 Jerry and Janie Murrell offered their sons a choice, college or a burger stand. They picked the stand. There are 250,000 ways to order, the fries are cooked in peanut oil, and the chain now has about 1,900 restaurants in nearly 30 countries.
Very simply put: the burger built on never discounting sells two for one, one day a year.

slides.headline: It started with a choice: *college or a burger stand*.
slides.sub: In 1986 Jerry and Janie Murrell offered their sons the tuition money to start a business instead. They chose burgers.

slides.headline: The five guys are *the sons*.
slides.sub: Jim, Matt, Chad, Ben and Tyler. Jerry counted himself until the fifth boy was born.

slides.headline: The fries are cooked in *peanut oil*.
slides.sub: Hand-cut. Free peanuts sit by the door.

slides.headline: There are *250,000 ways* to order the burger.

slides.headline: About *1,900 restaurants* in nearly 30 countries.
slides.sub: Most of them in the United States. The first one outside America opened in London on July 4, 2013.

slides.headline: The first *franchise* opened in 2003.
slides.sub: Seventeen years after the first store. The family still owns the company.
